findings.rule: Heat treatment field must not be blank when a heat-treatment note is specified on the drawing.
findings.reasoning: The title block heat_treatment field is '---' while note N1 explicitly requires case hardening to 55–60 HRC with a 0.8–2 mm case depth. A manufacturer reading only the title block would skip the required heat treatment entirely.
findings.correction: Update the title block heat_treatment field to reference N1 (e.g., 'CASE HARDEN 55-60 HRC, REF NOTE N1') or state the requirement directly.

findings.rule: Functional outer diameters of a precision sleeve require explicit tolerances or fit classes.
findings.reasoning: Dimensions D1 and D13 define the ⌀30 outer cylindrical surface (F1) of a pin sleeve but carry no tolerance. Under the general machining tolerance for 6–30 mm this yields ±0.5 mm, which is far too loose for a functional sleeve OD that likely mates with a housing bore.
findings.correction: Add an appropriate tolerance or fit class (e.g., h6, h7) to D1 and D13 to control the outer diameter for its mating function.

findings.rule: Threads running into a shoulder or blind bottom require an undercut or thread-relief; case-hardened threads need a soft-threads process callout.
findings.reasoning: Feature F4 describes a blind M5 × 6 deep threaded hole. No thread relief or undercut is dimensioned, making it impossible to cut full-depth threads without a tap crashing into the bottom. Additionally, N1 states 'THREADS TO BE KEEP SOFT', but no masking detail or process sequence is provided to prevent carburization of the thread during the 0.8–2 mm case-hardening cycle.
findings.correction: Add a thread-relief undercut or increase the drill depth beyond 6 mm so the tap can produce full threads. Specify copper plating/masking of the thread area before carburizing, or call out post-carburize machining to keep threads soft as required by N1.
